reviewer: Claude on mbp1, #774: transcript, request log, notes and production report
rule: An intervention is an action on the project or tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is an unresolved Ultima setup, theme or styling choice that changed the output. Product choices and documented alternatives do not count. Browser checks of the consumer application follow the guidance; rendering documentation to retrieve guidance or source would count.

interventions.action: Ran `npx ultima-design@latest init --help`. The CLI rejected it (`Unknown option '--help'`) and printed its usage.
interventions.reason: No guidance prints a help command, and the CLI does not accept one. The #810 Vite review counted the same probe.

notes: The agent fetched llms.txt, the install, update, build-a-screen, support and Recipes guides, and the projects, list-detail, interaction-states and product-tokens lessons over HTTP. It did not render documentation, decode a data link, extract a bundle, read CRM 01's registry source or reference the live host or another checkout. It ran init through --plan and --apply, installed the theme and components with the printed shadcn@4.21.4, imported the theme where the install guide prints, and set up ESLint by the documented project-without-ESLint path. Under the arrangement rule from #845, the app keeps `minBlockSize: '100dvh'` and its `minmax(0, …)` track templates literal in local StyleX, the breakpoint as a named constant in the screen file, and only `--app-size-content-max` in screen.stylex.ts (#845 holds). The browser check follows the printed hand step, so its playwright-core install, scripts and server port are not counted. Reading the built CSS carries out the printed cascade step. The self-reported decisions (font fallback, Select over Dialog, Badge tones, number Input, the optional agent setup) are documented options or product choices. Deleting init's setup-check preview after replacing page.tsx follows the starter comment. check, doctor, StyleX lint (0 errors) and the raw-paint scan passed. All four external production cases failed `axe-open` with `aria-hidden-focus` on Base UI's four focus-guard spans around the open Select. That is not an agent choice: Base UI's Select backdrop cuts out the trigger, this app's Category trigger lands on axe's bottom-right modal sample point at 1280x800, so axe's isModalOpen heuristic misses the backdrop and reports the guards as violations instead of the incompletes the runner reviews. Two re-measures of a copy gave the same result. No operator edited the app.
